A1.name: FRC.Pair.pair_register
A1.doc: 38:A1, 38:A2 — the pair `(13, 233)`: `p = 13 = 4·3 + 1`, `Ω = 233 = 4·58 + 1`, the drive `g = 2` (`pair_frame`), `i = 5 = −g³ = g⁹`, `i² = −1`, and the tower identity `g = 3·5` with `3 = g⁴`, `3³ = 1`, `5⁴ = 1`; the frame is `pair_frame`.

A2.name: FRC.Pair.tower_solvable
A2.doc: 38:A2 — the tower congruence `4a − κb = 1` is solvable for every odd `κ`: `(a, b) = ((3κ + 1)/4, 3)` for `κ ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and `((κ + 1)/4, 1)` for `κ ≡ 3 (mod 4)` — the instances `(1, 1)` at `κ = 3`, `(4, 3)` at `κ = 5`, `(2, 1)` at `κ = 7`.

A2.name: FRC.Subject.spinor
A2.doc: 38:A2, 00:F4, 00:F6 — **C16 (p00151), the spinor dichotomy**, on every frame (`p − 1 = 4κ`, `i = −g^κ`): `κ` is odd iff `v₂(p − 1) = 2` (`8 ∤ p − 1`) iff the fold `(r, s) ↦ iʳ (g⁴)ˢ` is injective on `C₄ × C_κ`, and then onto `𝔽_p^×`, so `C_{p−1} ≅ C₄ × C_κ`; and iff `3κr + 4s ≡ 1 (mod 4κ)` is solvable.

A2.name: FRC.Subject.two_part
A2.doc: 38:A2 — C16's 2-parts. With `p − 1 = 2^a u` and `Ω − 1 = 2^b w`, `u, w` odd, and `m = min(a, b)`: `2^m` divides both and `2^{m+1}` not both (the shared 2-part `C_{2^m}`), and `2^m · 2^{b−m} = 2^b` (the shared order times the cover degree is the Carrier's 2-part); for `Ω − 1 = 4S` the Carrier's 2-part is `8` iff `S ≡ 2 (mod 4)`.

A2.name: FRC.Pair.pair_register
A2.doc: 38:A1, 38:A2 — the pair `(13, 233)`: `p = 13 = 4·3 + 1`, `Ω = 233 = 4·58 + 1`, the drive `g = 2` (`pair_frame`), `i = 5 = −g³ = g⁹`, `i² = −1`, and the tower identity `g = 3·5` with `3 = g⁴`, `3³ = 1`, `5⁴ = 1`; the frame is `pair_frame`.

A3.name: FRC.Subject.channel
A3.doc: 38:A3, 22:A2, 22:P4 — **C20 (p00040), the mass–energy channel**, generator-free on a prime `p` with a quarter-turn `h² = −1`: inside `𝔽_{p²}^×`, `C_{p−1} = 𝔽_p^×` meets the boost torus `C_{p+1} = {z^{p+1} = 1}` in the sign `±1` alone, and the spinor cover `C_{2(p+1)}` in exactly `Q₄ = {±1, ±h}`; the quarter is spinorial, `N(h) = h^{p+1} = h² = −1`.

A3.name: FRC.Pair.channel_instance
A3.doc: 38:A3 — the channel at the instance: `gcd(12, 14) = 2`, `gcd(12, 28) = 4`, `N(i) = i² = −1` — as the divisor facts the kernel decides: `2 ∣ 12, 14` and no `d > 2` divides both; `4 ∣ 12, 28` and no `d > 4` divides both.

A4.name: FRC.Subject.channel_233
A4.doc: 38:A4 — C20's Carrier instance: on `Ω = 233`, `78^58 = 89 = ħ`, a root of `−1`.

A4.doc: 38:A4 — the Carrier frame `(233; 58, 78)` and its quarter roots: `78⁵⁸ = 89 = h`, `h² = −1`, `ħ = 144 = −h`, `ħh = 1`, `ħ + h = 0` (`= Ω`), `78¹¹⁶ = −1`, `78²³² = 1`; the octant `ζ₈ = 97`: `97² = 89`, `97⁴ = −1`, `97⁸ = 1`; the Fibonacci convergents `h = 13/8`, `ħ = 8/13` on `𝔽₂₃₃` and `233 = 13² + 8²`.

A7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.sphere_det
A7.doc: 38:A7 — the norm-one sphere is `SL₂`: with `r² = −1` the quaternion `x + y i + z j + w k` is the matrix `quat` (`1, i, j, k ↦ I, diag(r, −r), [[0, 1], [−1, 0]], [[0, r], [r, 0]]`) and its norm is the determinant.

A7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.quat_bijective
A7.doc: 38:A7 — the quaternion map is a bijection of `𝔽_p⁴` onto `M₂` on a field shell with `r² = −1` and `2h = 1`, the inverse `M ↦ ((a + d) h, (a − d)(−r) h, (b − c) h, (b + c)(−r) h)`: with `sphere_det`, the norm-one sphere is the whole of `SL₂`.

C13.name: FRC.Drift.nesting_bound
C13.doc: 38:C13 — **the apsidal bound is the nesting condition.** A nested Subject `p = q + 1` on a Carrier `Ω` registers the apsidal fraction `κ/S = (p − 1)/(Ω − 1)` (`Pair.leak_rate`), and the bound `κ/S < 1/(√Ω + 1)` is, squared and cleared of its root, `(p − 1)²Ω < (Ω − p)²`, which holds exactly when `p² < Ω`: with `Ω = p² + d`, `(Ω − p)² − (p − 1)²Ω = d(Ω − 1) > 0` for `d ≥ 1`, and with `p² = Ω + d`, `Ω = m + q + 1`, `(Ω − p)² + d(Ω − 1) = (p − 1)²Ω`, so the bound fails. On the physical Carrier no hosted Subject registers an observed precession (the paper's C13).

D7.name: FRC.Pair.covering_parity
D7.doc: 38:D12, 38:D7 — **the covering parity theorem** (Theorem *The covering parity theorem*, Lemma *The all-shell parity table*). On an odd prime shell `p`, a node of shell `a` and row `k` (`0 < a, k < p`) with `M = k a⁻¹` (`aM ≡ k`, `0 < M < p`) has the four candidate slots with wrap counts `A = ⌊aM/p⌋`, `B = ⌊(p − M)a/p⌋`, `C = ⌊M(p − a)/p⌋`, `D = ⌊(p − M)(p − a)/p⌋`, the quotients of the division algorithm. Then the reflection identity four ways, `A + B + 1 = a`, `A + C + 1 = M`, `C + D + 1 = p − a`, `B + D + 1 = p − M`; `aM = pA + k` exactly; and the multiplicity `μ = mu A B C D` of the node satisfies `μ = 3` exactly when `k` is even, `μ ∈ {1, 3}` (so no node is missed), and on an odd row the single match is direct (`A` even or `B` odd, parameter `a`) exactly when the shell `a` is odd.

D8.name: FRC.Pair.ramification

D9.name: FRC.Pair.fusion

D12.name: FRC.Pair.reflection_identity
D12.doc: 38:D12 — the reflection identity on a prime shell: for `0 < a, b < p` the quotients of `ab` and `(p − a)b` by `p` sum to `b − 1`, `⌊ab/p⌋ + ⌊(p − a)b/p⌋ + 1 = b`. The quotients are the division algorithm's: `ab = p q₁ + (ab mod p)` and `(p − a)b = p q₂ + ((p − a)b mod p)` (`FRC.Nat.mod_spec` names them, `quot_unique` makes them unique).

D12.name: FRC.Pair.parity_table
D12.doc: 38:D12 — the eight-case parity table, decided by the kernel on the residues: with `x = ā`, `y = M̄`, `z = α = A mod 2`, `u, v, t` the parities of `B, C, D` and `w = k̄`, the relations `k̄ = ā M̄ + α`, `A + B + 1 = a`, `A + C + 1 = M`, `C + D + 1 = p − a` force `μ = 3` exactly when `k̄ = 0`, `μ ∈ {1, 3}`, and on an odd row the single match is a direct slot (wrap `A` even or `B` odd, parameter `a`) exactly when `a` is odd.

D12.name: FRC.Pair.covering_parity
D12.doc: 38:D12, 38:D7 — **the covering parity theorem** (Theorem *The covering parity theorem*, Lemma *The all-shell parity table*). On an odd prime shell `p`, a node of shell `a` and row `k` (`0 < a, k < p`) with `M = k a⁻¹` (`aM ≡ k`, `0 < M < p`) has the four candidate slots with wrap counts `A = ⌊aM/p⌋`, `B = ⌊(p − M)a/p⌋`, `C = ⌊M(p − a)/p⌋`, `D = ⌊(p − M)(p − a)/p⌋`, the quotients of the division algorithm. Then the reflection identity four ways, `A + B + 1 = a`, `A + C + 1 = M`, `C + D + 1 = p − a`, `B + D + 1 = p − M`; `aM = pA + k` exactly; and the multiplicity `μ = mu A B C D` of the node satisfies `μ = 3` exactly when `k` is even, `μ ∈ {1, 3}` (so no node is missed), and on an odd row the single match is direct (`A` even or `B` odd, parameter `a`) exactly when the shell `a` is odd.
